question: What is the primary purpose of performing a liver biopsy?

options.A: Extracting hepatic tissue for microscopic examination
options.B: Draining infected abscesses from the right lobe

explanation: A liver biopsy involves obtaining a tissue sample to examine cells under a microscope for disease staging and diagnosis. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why is a liver biopsy ordered for a patient with long-term hepatitis?

options.A: To prevent swollen veins in the esophagus
options.B: To clear blockages in the main bile ducts
options.C: To check the level of liver inflammation and scarring
options.D: To stop the virus from multiplying in the blood

explanation: Examining liver tissue under a microscope allows clinicians to see how much damage and scarring (fibrosis) chronic disease has caused. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h1)

question: Which blood test results must you check before a patient has a liver biopsy?
explanation: Checking how well the blood clots and looking at platelet levels ensures the patient is safe from uncontrolled bleeding during the procedure. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h2)

question: Why does a large amount of fluid in the abdomen (ascites) make a liver biopsy dangerous?

options.A: It stops local numbing medicine from working
options.B: It causes the patient's blood pressure to drop suddenly
options.C: It speeds up how fast blood vessels clot
options.D: It makes the liver float away from the abdominal wall, making it hard to reach

explanation: Excess fluid in the belly causes the liver to shift around, increasing the chance of missing the target or accidentally injuring other organs. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h2)

question: What is the standard instruction regarding food and drink before a liver biopsy?

options.A: Do not eat or drink anything for six to eight hours
options.B: Avoid all dairy products for twenty-four hours
options.C: Drink at least one liter of water right before
options.D: Eat a heavy meal two hours before the procedure

explanation: Fasting before the procedure keeps the stomach empty, reducing the risk of vomiting and minimizing liver movement. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h3)

question: A patient asks why they need to practice holding their breath during a liver biopsy. What is the best response?

options.A: It relaxes your chest muscles so you feel no pain.
options.B: It lowers your blood pressure so you bleed less.
options.C: It helps the numbing medicine spread evenly.
options.D: It keeps the diaphragm still so the needle does not tear the liver tissue.

explanation: Holding the breath stops the diaphragm and liver from moving up and down, preventing accidental injury when the biopsy needle goes in. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h3)

question: How should a patient be positioned for a standard liver biopsy?

options.A: Lying on their left side with knees pulled up
options.B: Lying on their back with the right arm raised above the head
options.C: Lying face down with a pillow under the stomach
options.D: Sitting upright with legs hanging over the bed

explanation: Raising the right arm opens up the spaces between the ribs, giving the doctor easier access to the liver. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h4)

question: At what point in breathing should the patient hold their breath during the biopsy?

options.A: At the very end of a normal breath out
options.C: Halfway through taking a normal breath
options.D: At the deepest point of a big breath in

explanation: Breathing out pushes the diaphragm up, protecting the liver against the chest wall and making the procedure safer. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h4)

question: Why is a patient placed lying on their right side right after a liver biopsy?

options.A: To help the left lung expand fully
options.B: To help digestion and bile flow
options.C: To stop them from feeling dizzy
options.D: To put pressure on the biopsy site and prevent bleeding

explanation: Lying on the right side presses the liver against the abdominal wall, which helps seal the puncture site and stops bleeding. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h5)

question: A patient complains of mild right shoulder pain two hours after a liver biopsy. What does this mean?

options.A: Irritation of the diaphragm by blood or the needle
options.B: They are showing early signs of a heart attack
options.C: They are having an allergic reaction to the numbing drug
options.D: Their arm was placed in a bad position

explanation: The nerve that supplies the diaphragm also reaches the right shoulder, which is why irritation around the liver can cause pain felt in the shoulder. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h5)

question: Which sign is the most reliable early warning of internal bleeding after a liver biopsy?

options.A: Fast heart rate and falling blood pressure
options.B: A sudden spike in body temperature
options.C: No bowel sounds in the abdomen

explanation: When blood pressure drops and the heart rate goes up, it is often the first sign that the patient is losing blood internally. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h6)

question: Which complication should you suspect if a patient has trouble breathing and reduced breath sounds after a liver biopsy?

options.D: Blood clot in the portal vein

explanation: If the needle accidentally enters the chest cavity near the lungs during the procedure, it can cause air to leak and the lung to partially collapse. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h6)

question: What is an important activity rule for a patient recovering at home after a liver biopsy?

options.A: Stay in bed all day for forty-eight hours
options.B: Avoid heavy lifting and hard exercise for a week
options.C: Sleep lying completely flat on your back
options.D: Do not drink any water for three days

explanation: Strenuous activities raise pressure inside the belly, which can dislodge the blood clot at the biopsy site and cause delayed bleeding. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h7)

question: Why must a patient avoid drugs like aspirin and ibuprofen after a liver biopsy?

options.A: They cause severe liver damage within a day
options.B: They prevent blood from clotting normally and increase bleeding risk
options.C: They hide the early signs of a chest infection
options.D: They interfere with how local numbing drugs work

explanation: Pain relievers like ibuprofen and aspirin stop platelets from clumping together, which is very risky because the liver has a rich blood supply. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h7)
